findings.assumptions: Correctly declared: the rank-layer limit (Lemma 3.1 of [161]) is proved only for the 35-vertex complex, so for any other pattern it is an assumption of the transfer and the barrier is conditional on it; the o(1) error at finite q is outside scope. Unstated but necessary: that the construction's symmetrization (Proposition 3.5, which uses the specific index sets I,J of [161]'s pattern) and coordinate expansion extend to an arbitrary pattern, which is what the failure criterion partly covers but the applicability text asserts without support.

findings.mathematical_substance: The hypothesis is that the kernels of [161], Equation (3.6), have limiting moments given by a sign model whose nonconstant factors are indexed by pairs of points lying in two faces (4-cycles of the incidence pattern), so that for a girth-six pattern the leading-order limit of t(H,V_q) equals (E V_q)^{e(H)} for all finite data. This is a precise, testable statement with an explicit failure criterion (Lemma 3.2 not reducing the limit to sign-model averages for general patterns; misreading of (3.2)-(3.4)). The novelty study itself describes the barrier as following 'in a few lines' from (3.2) and (3.4). Two issues: (i) the full text of [161] is not in the supplied evidence; every statement about its equations is a paraphrase in the studies, so the central mechanism claim is an unsupported inference relative to this packet; (ii) the hypothesis wording 'each sign variable occurs in at most one factor, the sign model is identically 1' is internally unclear: if nonconstant factors are indexed by pairs in two faces and no such pairs exist, there are no factors at all, whereas 'occurs in at most one factor' suggests a cancellation argument that would need independence of signs and could also involve longer even cycles. The result must say which argument is meant and why longer even cycles (present in every girth-six pattern with a cycle) contribute nothing.
findings.necessity: Not necessary for the route: route-000001 can close without this node. Its justification is that [161] is the only known disproof mechanism and the problem study's item 3 identifies checking its transfer as the first thing to do on the negative side. The applicability text's claim that 'no argument either way has reached girth-six patterns' is inaccurate as stated: the problem study lists proved positive classes containing girth-six patterns (1-subdivisions of cliques, KNRS and Sidorenko graphs; incidence graphs of regular polytopes; graphs with a part of at most four vertices). The intended meaning (no argument reaches the general girth-six statement) should be written.
findings.novelty: The novelty study (digest 2694276a...) searched for applications of [161]'s construction to 4-cycle-free patterns: the arXiv window 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-21 is reported captured completely with no work on graph patterns, MathOverflow 515955 has no answer, and the tier-one barrier queries (arXiv complete 7/7, zbMATH complete 5/5, Crossref top 20) returned only sum-of-squares and norming barriers (Blekherman-Raymond-Singh-Thomas, Garg-Raymond-Redlich, Coregliano, Lee-Schülke, Kral et al.). Semantic Scholar was unavailable (HTTP 429) and is recorded as a gap. The observation is claimed as a method boundary, not a deep result; this framing is honest and no source in the packet contradicts it.

findings.root_connection: The node targets obligation-000003 (girth-six patterns outside C_2), a premise of route-000001 whose bridge is the C_2 case split; the claim digest matches obligation-000003 exactly. The contribution is negative-direction research: either a transfer of the [161] mechanism yielding a counterexample (which would settle the root statement) or a method-relative barrier. The barrier branch, by the proposal's own parent_effect, 'decides neither the premise nor the route'. The first checkpoint criterion nevertheless records a 'verified_obstruction' bound to route_id route-000001, i.e. against the positive route itself. The obstruction established by the barrier is against a hypothetical negative route (refutation via [161]) that does not exist in the record; attaching it to route-000001 contradicts the parent_effect and would misstate the planning state.
findings.scope: The task input domain is every girth-six pattern (in particular outside C_2) and every finite data of [161], Sections 3.2-3.5, so the barrier covers C_2 as well; this is consistent with parent_effect. However the hypothesis sentence 'The construction of [161] ... does not transfer to any girth-six pattern' overclaims relative to the success criterion, which is leading order only and conditional on the rank-layer limit. A deficit at lower order (the natural near-miss regime when leading order gives equality) is not excluded by the barrier, and the hypothesis must be restated to say so.
findings.significance: Modest and method-relative. The admissible class is the literal family of [161] with finite data; a barrier on it rules out the simplest transfer at leading order but not modified constructions (parity on larger configurations, longer cycles) or lower-order deficits. Its planning value is to redirect negative-direction effort; it contributes nothing to a proof of obligation-000003. The resource plan (retreat at 10 moves, 24 max) is proportionate to that value.

The hypothesis mixes two arguments: 'nonconstant factors are indexed by pairs in two faces' (so no factors exist on a girth-six pattern) and 'each sign variable occurs in at most one factor' (a cancellation-by-independence argument). The result must state which holds for a general pattern and why even cycles of length at least six, present in every girth-six pattern with a cycle, contribute no nonconstant term under Lemma 3.2's expansion and Proposition 3.5's symmetrization for arbitrary index sets.
